items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the criminal procedure law and the penal law, in relation to the treatment of certain persons aged sixteen or seventeen for certain prostitution offenses
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S6804

TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the criminal procedure law and the
penal law, in relation to the treatment of certain persons aged
sixteen or seventeen for certain prostitution offenses

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section one of the bill amends Section 170.30 of the criminal
procedure law (CPL) by adding a new subdivision 4 to provide that a
criminal court may dismiss, after arraignment upon an information, a
simplified information, a prosecutor's information or misdemeanor
complaint on a charge of prostitution pursuant to section 230.00 of
the penal law (PL) or loitering for the purposes of prostitution
pursuant to PL section 240.37(2), provided that the person does not
stand charged with loitering for the purpose of patronizing a
prostitute, where such offense allegedly occurred when the person was
sixteen or seventeen years of age, such charge in its discretion in
the interest of justice on the ground that a defendant participated in
services provided to him or her.

Section two amends section 170.80 of the criminal procedure law (CPL),
as added by chapter 555 of the laws of 2013, to provide:

*that a judge may, at any time at or after arraignment on a charge of
prostitution pursuant to PL section 230.00 or loitering for the
purposes of prostitution pursuant to PL section 240.37(2), provided
that the person does not stand charged with loitering for the purpose
of patronizing a prostitute, where such offense allegedly occurred
when the person was sixteen or seventeen years of age, (a)
conditionally convert such charge and retain it as a person in need of
supervision (PINS) proceeding and make such proceeding fully subject
to the provisions and grant any relief available under Article 7 of
the family court act (PCA), and/or (b) order the provision of any of
the specialized services enumerated in title 8-A of Article 6 of the
social services law (SSL), as may be reasonably available.

*in the event of a conviction by plea or verdict to such charge or
charges of prostitution or loitering for the purposes of prostitution
as described in this section, the court must find that the person is a
youthful offender for the purpose of such charge, provided, however,
that the available sentence shall be the sentence that may be imposed
for a violation as defined in PL section 10.00(3). In such case, the
records of the investigation and proceedings relating to such charge
shall be sealed in accordance with CPL section 720.35.

*when a charge of prostitution or loitering for the purposes of
prostitution has been conditionally converted to a PINS proceeding
pursuant to this section, the defendant shall be deemed a "sexually
exploited child" as defined in SSL section 447-A(1) and therefore
shall not be considered an adult for purposes related to the charges
in the PINS proceeding. FCA sections 781, 782, 782-A, 783 and 784
shall apply to any proceeding conditionally converted under this
section.

*the court after hearing from the parties shall state the condition or
conditions of such conversion, which may include the individual's


participation in specialized services provided pursuant to title 8-A
of SSL and other appropriate services available to PINS in accordance
with FCA Article 7.

*the procedure by which the court may at any time during the pendency
of the PINS proceeding or during any disposition thereof, but in no
event later than the individual's 18th birthday, restore the
accusatory instrument if the court is satisfied by competent proof
that the individual, without just cause, is not in substantial
compliance with the condition or conditions of the conversion. If the
court finds that the person did not substantially comply, it may
restore the accusatory instrument, modify the terms of conversion or
otherwise continue such terms as in its discretion it deems just and
proper. If the accusatory instrument is restored, the proceeding shall
continue in accordance with subdivision 2 of this section. If the
individual does not comply with services or does not return to court,
the individual shall be returned in accordance with the provisions of
FCA Article 7.

*at the conclusion of a PINS proceeding pursuant to this section, the
records of the investigation and proceedings relating to such
proceeding shall be sealed in accordance with CPL section 720.35.

Section three amends CPL section 720.15 by adding a new subdivision 4
to provide that notwithstanding any provision in this article, the
provisions of subdivisions one and two of such section requiring or
authorizing the accusatory instrument filed against a youth to be
sealed, and that the arraignment and all proceedings in the action be
conducted in private shall apply where a person is charged with
prostitution as defined in PL section 230.00 or loitering for the
purposes of prostitution as defined in PL section 240.37(2), provided
that the person does not stand charged with loitering for the purpose
of patronizing a prostitute, and such person is aged sixteen or
seventeen when such offense occurred, regardless of whether such
person (i) had prior to commencement of trial or entry of a plea of
guilty been convicted of a crime or found a youthful offender, or (ii)
subsequent to such conviction for prostitution or loitering for
prostitution is convicted of a crime or found a youthful offender.

Section four amends the CPL by adding a new section 720.25 to provide
that notwithstanding any inconsistent provisions of law, (a) where the
court is required to find a person is a youthful offender pursuant to
CPL section 170.80, the fact that such person has previously been
convicted of a crime or adjudicated a youthful offender shall not
prevent such person from being adjudicated a youthful offender as
required by such section, and (b) a youthful offender adjudication
pursuant to CPI section 170.80 shall not be considered in determining
whether a person is an eligible youth, or in determining whether to
find a person a youthful offender, in any subsequent youthful offender
adjudication.

Section five amends CPL section 720.35(1), as amended by section 87 of
subpart B of part C of chapter 62 of the laws of 2011, to provide that
a defendant for whom a youthful offender adjudication was substituted,
who was originally charged with prostitution as defined in PL section
230.00 or loitering for the purposes of prostitution as defined in PL
section 240.37(2), provided that the person does not stand charged


with loitering for the purpose of patronizing a prostitute, for an
offense allegedly committed when he or she was sixteen or seventeen
years of age, shall be deemed a "sexually exploited child" as defined
in SSL section 447-A(1) and therefore shall not be considered an adult
for purposes related to the charges in the youthful offender
proceeding or a proceeding under CPL section 170.80. Section six
amends PL section 60.02 by adding a new subdivision 4 to provide that
notwithstanding any other provision of law in this section, if the
sentence is to be imposed upon a youthful offender finding which has
been substituted for a conviction of prostitution or loitering for the
purposes of prostitution provided that the person does not stand
charged with loitering for the purpose of patronizing a prostitute,
and such offense occurred when the person was sixteen or seventeen
years of age, the court must impose a sentence authorized to be
imposed upon a person convicted of a violation as defined in PL
section 10.00(3) and where the court imposes a revocable sentence
authorized for a violation may order any of the specialized services
enumerated in Title 8-A of SST, or other appropriate services made
available to PINS in accordance with FCA Article 7.

Section seven provides for the effective date.

JUSTIFICATION:

Individuals under the age of sixteen who are arrested for prostitution
or loitering for the purposes of prostitution are treated in the
Family Court as sexually exploited children and are eligible for
service alter natives as opposed to juvenile delinquency
adjudications. While the definition of a sexually exploited child,
created in 2007 under the Safe Harbour for Exploited Children Act
(Safe Harbour Law), includes children under the age of eighteen, it
was not until 2013 that sixteen and seventeen year olds brought to
criminal court were offered similar service alternatives. Chapter 555
of the laws of 2013 (the "2013 law"), amending the CPL relating to the
treatment of persons aged sixteen or seventeen for certain
prostitution offenses, allows criminal court judges to convert charges
of sixteen and seventeen year olds for prostitution or loitering for
the purposes of prostitution and treat these persons as PINS rather
than as criminals and grant any relief available under FCA Article 7.

This bill builds upon the 2013 law to clarify the alternatives
available to a person aged sixteen or seventeen charged with
prostitution or loitering for the purposes of prostitution, provided
the person is not charged with loitering for the purpose of
patronizing a prostitute, and the consequences of each alternative.
The charge may be conditionally converted and retained by the court as
a PINS proceeding; the charge may proceed as a criminal case which may
lead to conviction by plea or verdict; or the person may be referred
by the court to services and the charge subsequently dismissed in the
court's discretion in the interest of justice on the ground that the
youth participated in the services provided to him or her. The bill
provides that if a charge has been converted to a PINS proceeding, at
any time during the PINS proceeding or the disposition of the
proceeding but not later than the person's eighteenth birthday, the
charge may be converted from a PINS proceeding back to a criminal
proceeding and sets forth with particularity the process for
conversion back. In the event of a conviction by plea or verdict to a


charge of prostitution or loitering for the purposes of prostitution,
the court must find that the person is a youthful offender for the
purpose of such charge.

Whether the charge is conditionally converted or not, the court may
order the provision of any specialized services provided under the
Safe Harbour Law as may be reasonably available. Where a charge is
dismissed in the interest of justice on the ground that the person
participated in services provided or in the event of a conviction by
plea or verdict to such charge, the hill provides for the sealing of
the records of the investigation and proceedings relating to such
charge in accordance with CPL section 720.35.

Where the youth is convicted by plea or verdict to a charge of
prostitution or loitering for purposes of prostitution (other than
patronizing a person for prostitution), the court must find that the
person is a youthful offender for the purpose of such charge. it is
intended that a youth will be afforded youthful offender status on
such charge in all situations (1) where the conviction on such charge
is the first instance in which the youth is convicted of a crime or is
found to be a youthful offender, or (2) where the youth had been
previously convicted or a crime or found to be a youthful offender. In
addition, the bill provides that in a subsequent proceeding in which
adjudication of such youth as a youthful offender is being considered,
a court must not consider the mandatory youthful offender finding on a
charge of prostitution or loitering for purposes of prostitution
(other than patronizing a person for prostitution) as required by this
bill in determining whether the youth is an eligible youth or youthful
offender in such subsequent proceeding. In effect, in adjudicating the
youth on the subsequent charge, the court will determine such youth's
status as a youthful offender as if there had not been a prior
youthful offender finding on a charge of prostitution or loitering for
prostitution (other than patronizing a person for prostitution).

Further, the legislation makes clear that a sixteen or seventeen year
old charged with prostitution or loitering for purposes of
prostitution (other than patronizing a person for prostitution) shall
be deemed a sexually exploited child as defined in SSL 447-A(I)
entitled to services available to such children.

The 2013 law as supplemented by this legislation treats with parity,
at long last, individuals aged sixteen and seventeen and those under
age sixteen charged with prostitution or loitering for purposes of
prostitution - as victims, in need of specialized services.

FISCAL IMPACT:

Minimal.

EFFECTIVE DATE:

This act shall take effect immediately.

summary: Relates to the treatment of certain persons aged sixteen or seventeen for certain prostitution offenses.
